newsitem.title: philippines: Manila shares close down, secondliners steal focus.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares close down, secondliners steal focus.

text.p: * Index ends 12.48 pnts down, 0.38 pct, at 3,279.82
Manila shares finished lower on Thursday with profit-taking in selected blue chips led by PLDT as investors showed indifference to the Dow and PLDT's rise in New York, traders said.

"Aside from the Dow and PLDT, there was an absence of positive news, so people decided to sell some blue chips and play was on secondliners and penny stocks," said Rudsend Alpay, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities.

"At least now we are seeing some respite from the speculative stocks since most secondliners like Metro Pacific and Kuok Philippines did well," said Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity.
Range-trading took place for most of the session but a late selling spurt in Meralco B shares further pulled down the index.

Index heavyweight PLDT which was expected by traders to lift the index shed 25 pesos to 1,580 pesos as investors said the runup of the issue on Wednesday due to news of its stock dividend was big enough to spur some profit-taking.
The market also failed to take its cue from the Dow Jones' 93-point gain on Wednesday.
Cellular phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp was battered as a result of its lower-than-expected earnings in 1996, traders said.
Losers outnumbered gainers 74 to 40 with 92 issues unchanged. All sectors fell. Volume was heavy at 13.8 billion shares worth 4.4 billion pesos.

"I think we will see continued accumulation on secondliners tommorrow and an uptick may be expected next week considering that we have been in negative territory for most of the week," said Lippo's Alpay.
